sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Thyroid Eye Disease (TED), or Graves' Ophthalmopathy, is an autoimmune inflammatory disorder affecting the retrobulbar extraocular muscles and orbital fat. Although TED is classically bilateral and symmetrical, up to 10-15% of patients present with marked asymmetric or strictly **unilateral proptosis**. The presence of high serum **Anti-TSH Receptor Antibodies (TRAb / TSI)** is highly pathognomonic, driving orbital fibroblast proliferation, glycosaminoglycan (GAG) deposition, and tissue remodeling regardless of systemic thyroid status (euthyroid, hyperthyroid, or hypothyroid).

sections.title: Key Risk Factors for Severe Disease
content: **Cigarette Smoking**: Strongest modifiable risk factor (8x risk of TED, 4x risk of severe progression, reduces immunosuppression efficacy).
**High TRAb / TSI Titers**: Direct correlation with Clinical Activity Score (CAS) and disease severity.
**Male Gender & Older Age (>60)**: Lower incidence, but significantly higher risk of severe, optic-threat disease.
**Radioactive Iodine (RAI) Therapy**: Can precipitate or exacerbate active TED without prophylactic oral steroid coverage.
**Uncontrolled Dysthyroidism**: Both severe hyperthyroidism and poorly managed hypothyroidism exacerbate orbital activity.

sections.title: Eyelid & Orbital Clinical Signs
content: **Dalrymple Sign**: Upper eyelid retraction in primary gaze (scleral show above superior limbus).
**Von Graefe Sign**: Eyelid lag on downgaze (upper lid lags behind movement of globe).
**Kocher Sign**: Staring and frightened appearance, especially on sudden fixation.
**Stellwag Sign**: Infrequent or incomplete blinking.
**Gifford Sign**: Difficulty everting the upper eyelid.
**Mobius Sign**: Inability to maintain convergence of the eyes.

sections.title: Diagnostic Evaluation & Workup
content: 1. **Serology**: TRAb / TSI (highest specificity), TSH, Free T3/T4, anti-TPO antibodies.
2. **Exophthalmometry**: Hertel exophthalmometer (>20mm abnormal in Caucasians, >22mm in African Americans, or >2mm asymmetry).

3. **Orbital Imaging (Non-contrast CT / MRI)**: CT confirms fusiform extraocular muscle belly enlargement with apical overcrowding and TENDON SPARING. MRI T2-weighted sequences assess muscle water content (active edema).
4. **Visual Function Testing**: Color vision (Ishihara/Farnsworth-Munsell), Automated Visual Fields (Humphrey 24-2 or 30-2), RAPD, and VEP to rule out subclinical Dysthyroid Optic Neuropathy (DON).

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Dysthyroid Optic Neuropathy (DON) & Emergencies
content: Unexplained decrease in visual acuity or progressive central/paracentral scotoma.
Dyschromatopsia (loss of color vision saturation, specifically red desaturation).
Presence of a Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect (RAPD) in asymmetric disease.
Optic disc swelling (edema) or marked optic disc pallor on fundoscopy.
Severe exposure keratopathy with corneal ulceration, stromal thinning, or impending perforation.

sections.title: EUGOGO Disease Severity & Management Algorithm
content: **Mild Active TED**: Conservative measures (artificial tears, head elevation, prism glasses), strict smoking cessation, daily Selenium supplementation (100 mcg BID for 6 months).
**Moderate-to-Severe Active TED (CAS ≥ 3)**: First-line medical therapy with IV Methylprednisolone pulses OR Targeted Biologic therapy (Teprotumumab). Orbital radiotherapy as adjunctive treatment.

**Sight-Threatening TED (DON or Severe Corneal Exposure)**: IMMEDIATE High-dose IV Methylprednisolone (500mg-1000mg daily for 3 consecutive days). If insufficient response within 2 weeks -> Urgent Surgical Orbital Decompression.
**Inactive Rehabilitation Phase (CAS < 3)**: Surgical rehabilitation step-by-step: 1. Orbital Decompression -> 2. Strabismus Surgery -> 3. Eyelid Retraction Repair & Blepharoplasty.

sections.title: Surgical Rehabilitation Sequence
content: **Step 1: Orbital Decompression**: Performed FIRST. Options include balanced 2-wall (medial + lateral), 3-wall (+ floor), or deep lateral wall rim-sparing decompression. Decompression alters extraocular muscle alignment.

**Step 2: Strabismus Surgery**: Performed SECOND (at least 3 months post-decompression). Recession of fibrotic extraocular muscles (typically Inferior Rectus and Medial Rectus) using adjustable sutures. NEVER perform muscle resections in TED.
**Step 3: Eyelid Retraction Repair**: Performed LAST. Levator recession, mullerectomy, or spacer grafts (bovine pericardium, hard palate) to restore normal upper/lower eyelid margins.

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
content: **OPTIC Phase 3 Trial (Teprotumumab)**: Demonstrated 83% proptosis reduction (≥2mm) vs 10% placebo, with significant CAS reduction and diplopia improvement.
**EUGOGO 2021 Updated Guidelines**: Reaffirmed IVMP as first-line for moderate-to-severe active disease, integrated Teprotumumab and Tocilizumab into second-line protocols.
**TORIGIN Trial (Tocilizumab)**: Confirmed significant reduction in CAS and proptosis in steroid-resistant active TED.
**VRDN-001 / Next-Gen IGF-1R Antibodies**: Subcutaneous short-infusion anti-IGF-1R mAbs currently in Phase 3 trials showing rapid proptosis response.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls for Practice & Exams
content: **Unilateral Presentation**: Always order TRAb/TSI; positive antibody serology avoids unnecessary invasive orbital biopsy in asymmetric TED.
**Muscle Belly vs Tendon**: CT/MRI key feature: TED enlarges muscle bellies and spares tendons ('coke-bottle' appearance), unlike IOIS which involves tendons.
**IOP Elevation**: IOP rises significantly in upgaze due to restricted inferior rectus muscle compression on the globe.
**Radioactive Iodine Caution**: Pre-treat patients with oral Prednisone (0.3-0.5 mg/kg/day starting 1-3 days post-RAI, tapered over 1-2 months) if active TED is present.
**Never Resect EOMs**: Surgical correction of strabismus in TED MUST involve muscle recessions only; resections worsen inflammation and restriction.

sections.title: Special Population Considerations
sections.content:
– **Pediatric TED**: Extremely rare and typically mild. Manifests primarily as eyelid retraction and mild proptosis. Managed conservatively; surgical decompression or IV steroids are almost never required as orbital expansion accommodates tissue swelling.
– **Pregnancy**: TED often improves during the 2nd/3rd trimesters due to physiological immune tolerance, but may flare post-partum. High-dose steroids can be used with caution; Teprotumumab is strictly **contraindicated** (embryofetal toxicity/teratogenic).
